system.name: TON 618
system.description: One of the most massive known black holes in the universe, 10.4 billion light-years away. Its event horizon alone spans roughly 2,600 AU — wider than the entire outer solar system — and it radiates with the power of 140 trillion Suns.

ton618-bh.name: TON 618
ton618-bh.description: A hyperluminous quasar powered by a 66-billion-solar-mass black hole — one of the largest ever measured. Its event horizon diameter of ~2,600 AU dwarfs the entire solar system. Light we observe from TON 618 today left before the Solar System even existed, when the universe was only about 3 billion years old.
ton618-bh.funFact: TON 618's black hole is so massive that if placed at the Sun's position, its event horizon would extend well past the orbit of Neptune — swallowing every planet in our solar system.
